audit_member_text: [L145-L167,L301-L315] (HIGH/parameter-order defect) The XBeach grid branch decides whether a depth file is required from par%hotstart before the hotstart parameter is read from params.txt, so a requested hotstart can follow stale/default state and unnecessarily require or load depfile.
dispositions.rationale: span-confirmed: The depfile requirement tests par%hotstart at L160, but the input value is not read until L312. Thus the decision uses the preexisting value (params.def L92 defaults it to -123), so hotstart=1 in params.txt cannot suppress this earlier depth-file requirement.

evidence_span.quote:
if (par%setbathy .ne. 1 .and. par%hotstart .ne. 1) then

            call check_file_length(par%depfile,par%nx+1,par%ny+1)

adversarial.rationale: Generated parameter declarations initialize hotstart to -123 (params.def:L92), not to the user's requested value. all_input tests it for depfile at L160 and reads hotstart only at L312, with no earlier hotstart assignment or caller pre-read; a normal fresh hotstart request therefore unnecessarily requires depfile.

audit_member_text: [L170-L175,L247-L266,L283-L296,L419-L434] (HIGH/advisory-only critical bounds) Critical positive quantities including dx, dy, dtheta, dtheta_s, tstop, gravity, and wave periods are read without strict=.true., so zero or negative out-of-range values only warn and can later drive divisions, invalid extents, or nonterminating angle normalization.
dispositions.rationale: span-confirmed: The cited reads omit strict, and readkey_dbl defaults strict to false and only warns for out-of-range values (readkey.F90 L95-L125). This permits zero/negative physical inputs, including zero directional spacing used as a divisor at params.F90 L1380 and initialize.F90 L317; this confirms the input-validation defect without assuming every listed downstream consequence occurs.

evidence_span.quote:
par%dtheta_s   = readkey_dbl ('params.txt','dtheta_s',    10.d0,      0.1d0,   20.d0,required=.true.)
         else
            par%dtheta   = readkey_dbl ('params.txt','dtheta',    10.d0,      0.1d0,   180.d0,required=.true.)
         endif

adversarial.rationale: The advisory bounds really permit zero/negative gravity, periods and active grid spacings to reach unsafe arithmetic, but some negative dx/dy values intentionally request metric fallback on variable grids. The claimed nonterminating angular normalization is not established by these parameters: its increment is the fixed positive px constant; retain the concrete HIGH division/invalid-grid failures.

When the corresponding output is enabled, timestep_init divides by tintg/tintp/tintm/tinth at L201/L239/L277/L320 before any resulting-count checks; tint can supply the zero default for tintg.

audit_member_text: [L1536-L1538] (LOW/nonlinear option coercion) Every posdwn value below 0.1, including allowed small positive values, is coerced to -1 while other positive magnitudes remain unnormalized, making this nominal sign option behave discontinuously.
dispositions.rationale: span-confirmed: The allowed numeric interval for posdwn includes small positive values, yet this block maps every value below 0.1 to -1 and leaves the others unchanged. The backward-compatibility comment explains accepting zero but does not neutralize the discontinuous treatment of positive values such as 0.05 versus 0.1.

evidence_span.quote:
if (par%posdwn<0.1d0) then
         par%posdwn=-1.d0  ! Backward compatibility, now posdwn = 0 also works in input (i.e. posdwn = false)
      endif

adversarial.rationale: The parser accepts fractional posdwn values and the later <0.1 conversion changes their sign semantics discontinuously. No discrete-sign validation or normalization of the remaining positive values follows, and grid_bathy then multiplies depth by the resulting magnitude squared.
